days.title: The Value of the AWS Cloud: Benefits, Deployment Models, and Service Models

concepts.heading: The Six Advantages of Cloud Computing
concepts.body: AWS describes six advantages that appear again and again on CLF-C02: trade fixed expense for variable expense, benefit from massive economies of scale, stop guessing capacity, increase speed and agility, stop spending money running and maintaining data centers, and go global in minutes. Trading fixed for variable expense means you pay for servers by the second or hour instead of buying hardware years in advance. Economies of scale means AWS buys and runs hardware for millions of customers, so its per-unit costs are lower than a single company could reach, and those savings show up as lower prices. Stop guessing capacity means you no longer have to buy for the busiest day of the year and leave servers idle the rest of the time. Learn the exact wording of all six, because exam choices often quote them almost word for word.

concepts.heading: Speed, Agility, and Going Global
concepts.body: Agility means new resources are a few clicks or one API call away, so a team can launch a test environment in minutes instead of waiting weeks for a hardware order. Because experiments are cheap and fast, companies can try more ideas and throw away the ones that fail without being stuck with purchased equipment. Going global in minutes means you can deploy the same application in AWS Regions on other continents to serve users with lower latency. For example, a startup in Seoul can add a copy of its web application in Frankfurt for European customers without building a data center there. Questions that mention faster time to market or experimentation point to speed and agility.

concepts.heading: Elasticity, Scalability, and High Availability
concepts.body: Scalability is the ability of a system to handle growth, either by adding bigger resources (vertical scaling) or more resources (horizontal scaling). Elasticity goes one step further: capacity grows and shrinks automatically with demand, so you are not paying for idle servers after a traffic spike ends. High availability means the application keeps running when a component fails, usually by spreading copies across multiple Availability Zones. Fault tolerance is the stricter idea that users notice no interruption at all when something breaks. On the exam, automatic adding and removing of capacity is elasticity, while surviving failures is availability or fault tolerance.

concepts.heading: Cloud Deployment Models
concepts.body: A cloud (or cloud-native) deployment runs all parts of the application in the cloud, either built there from the start or migrated from on premises. A hybrid deployment connects cloud resources to infrastructure that stays in a company's own data center, for example a web tier in AWS that reads from a database kept on premises for regulatory reasons. An on-premises deployment, sometimes called a private cloud, uses virtualization and resource management tools in the company's own data center. AWS supports hybrid designs with services such as AWS Direct Connect, AWS Site-to-Site VPN, and AWS Outposts. If a question describes keeping some systems in the company data center while using AWS for others, the answer is hybrid.

concepts.heading: IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS
concepts.body: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) gives you the basic building blocks, such as virtual servers, storage, and networking, and you manage the operating system and everything above it; Amazon EC2 is the classic example. Platform as a Service (PaaS) removes the need to manage the underlying servers and operating systems so you can focus on deploying your code; AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a common example. Software as a Service (SaaS) is a complete product run by the provider that you simply use, such as a web-based email or CRM application. The further you move from IaaS to SaaS, the less you manage and the less control you have. This idea connects directly to the shared responsibility model you will study in Domain 2.

examPoints: When a question describes avoiding a large up-front hardware purchase and paying only for what is used, pick trade fixed expense for variable expense; when it describes lower prices because AWS operates at huge volume, pick benefit from massive economies of scale.

When a question describes capacity that automatically increases during a spike and decreases afterwards, pick elasticity; when it describes keeping the application running after a server or data center fails, pick high availability or fault tolerance instead.

quiz.q: A company no longer wants to buy servers three years in advance and would rather pay monthly only for the compute it actually uses. Which advantage of cloud computing does this describe?
choices: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
quiz.explain: Replacing an up-front capital purchase with pay-as-you-go spending is trading fixed expense for variable expense. Economies of scale is tempting because it is also about cost, but it describes AWS's lower unit prices from serving many customers, not the shift away from up-front buying.

quiz.q: An online shop's web tier adds servers automatically during a holiday sale and removes them when traffic returns to normal. Which cloud concept is this?
quiz.explain: Automatically matching capacity to demand in both directions is elasticity. High availability is tempting because more servers can also help resilience, but it is about surviving failures, not about scaling up and down with traffic.

days.recap: The cloud's value comes from six advantages (variable expense, economies of scale, no capacity guessing, agility, no data center upkeep, global reach), delivered through cloud, hybrid, or on-premises deployments and IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS service models.

days.title: The AWS Well-Architected Framework: Six Pillars and Design Principles

concepts.heading: What the Well-Architected Framework Is
concepts.body: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is a set of best practices and questions that help you evaluate whether a workload is secure, reliable, efficient, cost-effective, and sustainable. It is organized into six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. The free AWS Well-Architected Tool in the console lets you answer the framework's questions for a workload and get a list of improvement items. The framework does not certify or approve an architecture; it is a self-review guide. On CLF-C02 you mainly need to match a described goal to the correct pillar.

concepts.heading: Operational Excellence and Security
concepts.body: Operational Excellence is about running and monitoring systems and continually improving processes, for example performing operations as code, making frequent small reversible changes, and learning from operational failures. Security is about protecting data, systems, and assets: applying least-privilege access, enabling traceability with logging, protecting data in transit and at rest, and preparing for security events. A team that automates deployments with templates and reviews incidents to prevent repeats is practicing Operational Excellence. A team that encrypts data and limits who can access it is following the Security pillar. The keywords are automate, observe, and improve for Operational Excellence, and protect, encrypt, and trace for Security.

concepts.heading: Reliability and Performance Efficiency
concepts.body: Reliability is the ability of a workload to perform its intended function correctly and consistently, including recovering automatically from failure and scaling to meet demand. Typical reliability practices are deploying across multiple Availability Zones, testing recovery procedures, and keeping backups. Performance Efficiency is about using computing resources efficiently as demand and technology change, for example choosing the right instance type, using serverless services, or putting content close to users with Amazon CloudFront. A good way to separate them is that Reliability asks whether the system keeps working, while Performance Efficiency asks whether it uses the best resources for the job. Both pillars mention scaling, so read the question for the main goal: recovery points to Reliability, speed and right resource choice point to Performance Efficiency.

concepts.heading: Cost Optimization and Sustainability
concepts.body: Cost Optimization is about delivering business value at the lowest price point: paying only for what you use, measuring spend, rightsizing instances, and using pricing models such as Savings Plans or Spot Instances. Sustainability, the newest pillar, focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads, for example maximizing utilization so fewer resources sit idle and choosing efficient managed services. The two pillars often recommend the same actions, because turning off idle servers saves both money and energy. On the exam, a question that mentions carbon footprint, energy use, or environmental impact is Sustainability, even if the action would also save money. A question that focuses on reducing the bill is Cost Optimization.

concepts.heading: General Design Principles
concepts.body: Alongside the pillars, the framework lists general design principles that summarize good cloud architecture. They include stop guessing your capacity needs, test systems at production scale, automate to make experimentation easier, allow for evolutionary architectures, drive architectures using data, and improve through game days that simulate failures. Other widely taught principles are design for failure, decouple components so one failure does not cascade, and think parallel rather than relying on one big server. For example, putting an Amazon SQS queue between a web tier and a processing tier is loose coupling, because each side can fail or scale independently. These principles appear in questions that ask which practice best follows AWS architectural guidance.

examPoints: When a question mentions reducing environmental impact or energy consumption of a workload, pick the Sustainability pillar, not Cost Optimization, even if the action also saves money.

When a question describes recovering from failure, multi-AZ deployments, or testing recovery procedures, pick Reliability; when it describes choosing the best instance type or technology for speed, pick Performance Efficiency.

quiz.q: A company wants to reduce the carbon footprint of its workloads by increasing server utilization and removing idle resources. Which Well-Architected pillar does this goal belong to?
quiz.explain: Reducing environmental impact is the focus of the Sustainability pillar. Cost Optimization is tempting because removing idle resources also saves money, but the stated goal here is carbon footprint, which is what Sustainability covers.

quiz.q: A workload must automatically recover from the failure of a single data center and continue serving customers. Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework does this requirement relate to most directly?
quiz.explain: Recovering from failure and continuing to function correctly is the core of the Reliability pillar. Performance Efficiency is tempting because it also involves architecture choices, but it is about using resources efficiently for speed, not about surviving failures.

days.recap: The Well-Architected Framework has six pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability), and most exam questions simply ask you to match a goal to its pillar.

days.title: Migration to the Cloud and Cloud Economics: AWS CAF, the 7 Rs, and TCO

concepts.heading: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)
concepts.body: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework helps organizations plan a cloud transformation and groups the needed capabilities into six perspectives. The Business, People, and Governance perspectives focus on business capabilities, while Platform, Security, and Operations focus on technical capabilities. People covers culture, training, and organizational change; Governance covers managing risk, portfolio, and cloud spending; Platform covers building the cloud environment and architecture; Operations covers running and monitoring workloads day to day. AWS CAF also describes benefits of a transformation, such as reduced business risk, improved environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, increased revenue, and increased operational efficiency. A question about training staff and managing organizational change points to the People perspective.

concepts.heading: The 7 Rs Migration Strategies
concepts.body: AWS describes seven common strategies for moving applications. Rehost (lift and shift) moves an application to Amazon EC2 without changes; Replatform (lift, tinker, and shift) makes small optimizations such as moving a database to Amazon RDS; Refactor (or re-architect) redesigns the application with cloud-native features such as serverless. Repurchase replaces the application with a different product, often SaaS; Relocate moves an entire virtualized environment, for example VMware workloads, to the cloud without buying new hardware; Retain keeps an application where it is for now; Retire switches off applications that are no longer needed. Rehost is usually fastest, while Refactor takes the most effort but can deliver the most cloud benefit. Learn the short descriptions, because questions describe the action and ask for the strategy name.

concepts.heading: Migration Services
concepts.body: AWS Application Migration Service is the recommended way to rehost servers: it continuously replicates source servers to AWS and then launches them as EC2 instances at cutover. AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) moves databases to AWS with minimal downtime, and its schema conversion feature helps when the source and target engines differ, such as Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. AWS DataSync copies large amounts of file and object data between on-premises storage and AWS storage services over the network, and AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP and FTPS endpoints into Amazon S3. For very large transfers, a dedicated AWS Direct Connect link gives a steadier, higher-bandwidth path than the public internet. Note that the AWS Snowball Edge devices and AWS Migration Hub that appear in older study materials are no longer open to new customers.

concepts.heading: Cloud Economics and Total Cost of Ownership
concepts.body: Total cost of ownership (TCO) compares the full cost of running a workload on premises with running it in AWS, including items people often forget. On-premises fixed costs include hardware, data center space, power, cooling, and the staff time to rack servers and replace failed disks. In AWS, much of that becomes a variable cost, and staff can move from undifferentiated heavy lifting to work that helps the business. Rightsizing, which means choosing the smallest instance type that meets performance needs, is one of the quickest ways to lower cloud cost. When a question asks about the hidden savings of moving to AWS, think of reduced operational and labor costs as well as hardware.

concepts.heading: Licensing and Ownership Choices
concepts.body: When moving software such as Windows Server or SQL Server, you can either use license-included instances, where the license cost is built into the hourly price, or bring your own license (BYOL) if your existing licenses allow it. BYOL can lower cost when you already own licenses, and some licenses are tied to physical cores, which is one reason to use Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts. Managed services also change the economics, because AWS handles patching, backups, and hardware, which lowers operational effort. For example, moving a self-managed database from EC2 to Amazon RDS reduces the hours staff spend on database maintenance. Exam questions in this area test that you understand which costs disappear and which remain after migration.

examPoints: When a question describes moving an application to AWS exactly as it is, with no code changes, pick Rehost (lift and shift); when it describes swapping a self-managed database for Amazon RDS with only small changes, pick Replatform.
When a question asks which AWS CAF perspective covers staff skills, training, and organizational culture, pick People; when it covers managing risk and cloud spending, pick Governance.

quiz.q: A company wants to move its on-premises application servers to Amazon EC2 as quickly as possible without changing any code. Which migration strategy is this?
quiz.explain: Moving servers unchanged to EC2 is Rehost, often called lift and shift. Replatform is tempting because it also keeps the application mostly the same, but it involves small optimizations such as switching to a managed database, which the company is not doing.

quiz.q: During cloud adoption planning, a company focuses on training its staff in cloud skills and managing the cultural change across teams. Which AWS CAF perspective does this work belong to?
quiz.explain: Training, skills, and organizational change belong to the People perspective. Governance is tempting because it also deals with organization-wide topics, but it covers risk management, portfolio management, and controlling cloud spending, not staff skills.

days.recap: AWS CAF organizes cloud adoption into six perspectives, the 7 Rs name the ways to move each application, and good cloud economics count labor, licensing, and rightsizing as well as hardware.

days.title: The AWS Shared Responsibility Model

concepts.heading: Security of the Cloud vs Security in the Cloud
concepts.body: The shared responsibility model divides security work between AWS and the customer. AWS is responsible for security of the cloud: the physical data centers, hardware, networking infrastructure, and the virtualization layer that runs AWS services. The customer is responsible for security in the cloud: their data, who can access it, how resources are configured, and, where applicable, the guest operating system and applications. For example, AWS guards the building and destroys old disks, while the customer decides whether an Amazon S3 bucket is public. Remember the short phrases of and in, because many questions are built directly on them.

concepts.heading: How Responsibility Shifts by Service Type
concepts.body: The line moves depending on how managed a service is. With Amazon EC2, an infrastructure service, the customer patches the guest operating system, installs and updates applications, and configures security groups. With Amazon RDS, AWS also patches the database engine and the underlying operating system, while the customer manages database users, network access, and encryption choices. With AWS Lambda, AWS manages the servers and runtime environment, and the customer is responsible mainly for the function code, its permissions, and its data. The more managed the service, the more AWS takes on, but the customer always keeps responsibility for data and access.

concepts.heading: What the Customer Always Owns
concepts.body: No matter which service you use, some responsibilities never move to AWS. The customer always controls their data, including classifying it and deciding whether to encrypt it. The customer always controls identity and access management: which users and roles exist and what they are allowed to do. The customer is also responsible for configuring services correctly, such as turning on encryption or blocking public access to an S3 bucket. A common exam trap is a choice suggesting that AWS will notice and fix a customer's misconfigured permissions; AWS provides tools to help, but the decision and the fix are the customer's.

concepts.heading: Shared Controls
concepts.body: Some controls are shared, meaning each side handles them in its own layer. Patch management is shared: AWS patches the infrastructure, and the customer patches guest operating systems and applications. Configuration management is shared: AWS configures its infrastructure devices, and the customer configures their own operating systems, databases, and applications. Awareness and training is also shared: AWS trains its employees, and the customer must train its own staff. Questions sometimes ask which control is shared, and patching is the most common example.

concepts.heading: What AWS Always Owns
concepts.body: Physical security of facilities, including guards, access badges, and video surveillance, is always AWS's job. AWS also maintains the hardware, replaces failed components, and securely destroys storage devices at the end of their life. The global network between AWS data centers and the hypervisor that isolates customer instances from each other are AWS responsibilities. Customers cannot visit AWS data centers to audit them; instead they download AWS's third-party audit reports from AWS Artifact, which you will study later this week. If a choice mentions hardware, facilities, or the global network, it belongs to AWS.

examPoints: When a question asks who patches the guest operating system on Amazon EC2, pick the customer; when it asks who patches the database engine on Amazon RDS or the servers behind AWS Lambda, pick AWS.

When a question asks about physical security, hardware disposal, or the global network, pick AWS; when it asks about data, encryption settings, IAM permissions, or security group rules, pick the customer.

quiz.q: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who is responsible for applying security patches to the guest operating system of an Amazon EC2 instance?
choices: The AWS Partner that published the Amazon Machine Image
No one, because EC2 instances patch themselves automatically
quiz.explain: EC2 is an infrastructure service, so the customer owns the guest operating system and must patch it. AWS is tempting because it patches the underlying host and hypervisor, but anything inside the instance is security in the cloud and belongs to the customer.

quiz.q: A company runs a database on Amazon RDS. Which task remains the customer's responsibility?
choices: Replacing failed physical disks in the storage layer
Controlling who can connect to the database through security groups and database users
quiz.explain: Network access rules and database user accounts are customer configuration, which stays with the customer even on a managed service. Patching the database engine is tempting, but on Amazon RDS AWS applies engine and operating system patches during the maintenance window the customer chooses.

days.recap: AWS secures the cloud itself (facilities, hardware, network, managed service infrastructure) and the customer secures what they put in it (data, access, configuration), with the split shifting toward AWS as services become more managed.

days.title: Identity and Access Management: Root User, IAM, and IAM Identity Center

concepts.heading: Protecting the Root User
concepts.body: The root user is the identity created with the email address used to open an AWS account, and it has complete, unrestricted access to everything in that account. AWS recommends turning on multi-factor authentication (MFA) for the root user, not creating access keys for it, and using it only for the few tasks that require it. Examples of root-only tasks are changing the account's root email address or password, closing the account, and restoring permissions when an administrator accidentally locks everyone out. For daily work, people should sign in with identities that have only the permissions they need. If a question asks about the very first step after creating an account, securing the root user with MFA is the answer.

concepts.heading: IAM Users, Groups, Roles, and Policies
concepts.body: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls who can do what in an account. An IAM user is a long-term identity with its own credentials, an IAM group is a collection of users that share the same permissions, and an IAM role is an identity with temporary credentials that a person, application, or AWS service can assume. Permissions are written in JSON policies that allow or deny specific actions on specific resources. For example, an application running on EC2 should use an IAM role attached to the instance rather than stored access keys, because the role's credentials rotate automatically. IAM is a global service and has no extra charge.

concepts.heading: Least Privilege and Multi-Factor Authentication
concepts.body: The principle of least privilege means granting only the permissions needed to perform a task, and nothing more. In practice you start with narrow permissions, use AWS managed policies or carefully written custom policies, and review unused permissions regularly; IAM Access Analyzer can help find access that is broader than intended. Multi-factor authentication adds a second check, such as an authenticator app or a hardware security key, so a stolen password alone is not enough to sign in. A strong password policy and regular review of credential reports also support good hygiene. Exam questions often ask for the best practice, and least privilege plus MFA is nearly always part of it.

concepts.heading: IAM Identity Center and Federation
concepts.body: AWS IAM Identity Center is the recommended way to give a workforce single sign-on access to multiple AWS accounts and business applications. It can use its own user directory or connect to an existing identity provider such as Microsoft Active Directory, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID, so employees sign in with their company credentials. Administrators assign permission sets that grant access to specific accounts in AWS Organizations. Federation in general means trusting an external identity provider instead of creating separate IAM users. Do not confuse this with Amazon Cognito, which handles sign-up and sign-in for the end users of your own web and mobile applications.

concepts.heading: Managing Credentials and Secrets
concepts.body: Access keys let programs and the AWS CLI call AWS APIs, and they should be rotated, never shared, and never written into source code. AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets such as database passwords and API keys, encrypts them, and can rotate them automatically on a schedule. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store can also hold configuration values and secrets, but automatic rotation is a Secrets Manager feature. For example, an application can fetch its database password from Secrets Manager at startup, so the password never appears in code or configuration files. When a question asks how to stop hardcoding database credentials and rotate them automatically, Secrets Manager is the answer.

examPoints: When a question asks how an application on Amazon EC2 or AWS Lambda should get permission to call other AWS services, pick an IAM role, never stored access keys or the root user.

When a question asks how employees can use their existing corporate credentials to sign in once and reach many AWS accounts, pick IAM Identity Center; pick Amazon Cognito only when the users are customers of the company's own application.

quiz.q: An application running on an Amazon EC2 instance needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to grant this access?
choices: Store an IAM user's access keys in the application's configuration file
Use the root user's access keys
Attach an IAM role with the required S3 permissions to the EC2 instance
Make the S3 bucket public so no credentials are needed
quiz.explain: An IAM role attached to the instance provides temporary credentials that rotate automatically and can be limited to exactly the needed permissions. Storing an IAM user's access keys is tempting because it works, but long-term keys in files can leak and must be rotated by hand.

quiz.q: A company wants employees to sign in once with their existing corporate directory credentials and then access several AWS accounts in its organization. Which service should it use?
choices: Create a separate IAM user for each employee in every account
quiz.explain: IAM Identity Center provides workforce single sign-on across AWS accounts and can connect to an existing corporate identity provider. Amazon Cognito is tempting because it also handles sign-in, but it is designed for the customers of your own applications, not employees accessing AWS accounts.

days.recap: Lock away the root user with MFA, give people and applications least-privilege access through IAM roles, groups, and policies, use IAM Identity Center for workforce sign-in, and keep secrets in AWS Secrets Manager.

days.title: Governance, Compliance, and Encryption: Artifact, CloudTrail, Config, Organizations, and KMS

concepts.heading: Compliance Reports with AWS Artifact
concepts.body: AWS participates in many compliance programs, such as SOC 1, SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and services that are HIPAA eligible. AWS Artifact is the self-service portal where you download AWS's security and compliance reports and accept agreements such as the Business Associate Addendum (BAA) used for HIPAA. Auditors often ask for these reports as evidence that the AWS side of the shared responsibility model is properly controlled. Using a compliant service does not automatically make your workload compliant, because you still have to configure your part correctly. Whenever a question mentions downloading a SOC report or PCI attestation for an auditor, the answer is AWS Artifact.

concepts.heading: CloudTrail, Config, and CloudWatch
concepts.body: These three services are easy to mix up, so learn one question each one answers. AWS CloudTrail answers who did what and when: it records API calls and console actions, such as which user terminated an instance or deleted a bucket. AWS Config answers what a resource looked like and whether it follows the rules: it records configuration history and evaluates resources against rules, such as flagging any S3 bucket without encryption. Amazon CloudWatch answers how resources are performing: it collects metrics and logs and triggers alarms, such as alerting when CPU usage stays above 80 percent. Auditing user activity is CloudTrail, compliance of settings is Config, and performance monitoring is CloudWatch.

concepts.heading: Multi-Account Governance with AWS Organizations and AWS Control Tower
concepts.body: AWS Organizations lets a company manage many AWS accounts centrally, grouping them into organizational units (OUs) such as Production and Development. Service control policies (SCPs) set the maximum permissions available in member accounts; for example, an SCP can stop anyone in development accounts from using Regions outside Europe, even administrators. SCPs do not grant permissions themselves, they only limit what IAM policies can allow. AWS Control Tower builds on Organizations to set up a well-governed multi-account environment, called a landing zone, with preconfigured guardrails called controls. Organizations also provides consolidated billing, which you will cover on the billing day.

concepts.heading: Encryption at Rest and in Transit
concepts.body: Encryption at rest protects stored data, such as objects in Amazon S3 or data on Amazon EBS volumes, while encryption in transit protects data moving across a network, usually with TLS. AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) creates and controls the encryption keys used by most AWS services, and every key use can be logged in CloudTrail. AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules for customers whose rules require full control of the key hardware. AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions and renews free public TLS certificates for use with services such as Elastic Load Balancing and Amazon CloudFront. Turning encryption on and managing key permissions is a customer responsibility.

concepts.heading: Logging, Reporting, and Evidence
concepts.body: Governance depends on keeping records that show controls are working. CloudTrail logs can be delivered to an S3 bucket and retained for years, which helps with investigations and audits. AWS Config keeps a timeline of configuration changes so you can see when a security group was opened and by which change. CloudWatch Logs collects application and system logs in one place for searching and alarms. Together with AWS Artifact reports for the AWS side, these records give auditors evidence for both halves of the shared responsibility model.

examPoints: When a question asks how to find out which user made a specific API call or deleted a resource, pick AWS CloudTrail; when it asks how to check whether resource settings comply with rules over time, pick AWS Config.

When a question mentions an auditor needing AWS's SOC or PCI reports, pick AWS Artifact; when it mentions creating and controlling encryption keys, pick AWS KMS (or AWS CloudHSM if dedicated single-tenant hardware is required).

quiz.q: An external auditor asks a company for AWS's SOC 2 report to review the controls AWS operates. Where can the company obtain it?
quiz.explain: AWS Artifact is the portal for downloading AWS's compliance reports, including SOC reports. AWS Config is tempting because it is also used for compliance, but it evaluates the customer's own resource settings and does not provide AWS's audit reports.

quiz.q: A security team needs to identify which IAM user deleted an Amazon S3 bucket yesterday. Which service provides this information?
quiz.explain: CloudTrail records API activity, including the identity that made each call and when, so it shows who deleted the bucket. AWS Config is tempting because it tracks resource changes, but its focus is the configuration state of resources rather than an audit trail of which user performed each action.

days.recap: AWS Artifact proves AWS's side of compliance, CloudTrail records who did what, Config tracks whether settings follow the rules, Organizations SCPs set account-wide limits, and KMS manages the keys that encrypt your data.

days.title: Threat Detection and Network Protection: GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Shield, and WAF

concepts.heading: GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie
concepts.body: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously analyzes sources such as CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs to find suspicious activity, for example an instance communicating with a known malicious IP address or unusual API calls from an unfamiliar location. Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, covering EC2 instances, container images in Amazon ECR, and Lambda functions. Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and protect sensitive data, such as personally identifiable information (PII) or credit card numbers, stored in Amazon S3. A simple memory aid is that GuardDuty watches behavior, Inspector checks for vulnerable software, and Macie finds sensitive data in S3. All three are managed and turn on with a few clicks.

concepts.heading: Detective and Security Hub CSPM
concepts.body: Amazon Detective helps investigate security findings by organizing log data into visual graphs, so an analyst can see the history behind a GuardDuty alert and find its root cause. AWS Security Hub CSPM (the original AWS Security Hub, now named for cloud security posture management) runs automated checks against best-practice standards and gathers findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and partner tools into one view. Its checks include standards such as the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices and CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Think of Security Hub CSPM as the central dashboard and Detective as the investigation tool. A question about a single place to see security findings across accounts points to Security Hub CSPM.

concepts.heading: AWS Shield and AWS WAF
concepts.body: AWS Shield protects against distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks. Shield Standard is automatically included at no extra cost for all customers and defends against common network and transport layer attacks. Shield Advanced is a paid service that adds enhanced detection, access to the AWS Shield Response Team, and cost protection against scaling charges caused by an attack. AWS WAF is a web application firewall that filters HTTP and HTTPS requests to Amazon CloudFront, Application Load Balancers, and Amazon API Gateway, using rules that block patterns such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting, or requests from certain countries. AWS Firewall Manager applies WAF rules, Shield Advanced protections, and security group policies consistently across all accounts in an organization.

concepts.heading: Security Groups vs Network ACLs
concepts.body: A security group is a virtual firewall for an instance or other resource; it supports only allow rules and is stateful, meaning that if inbound traffic is allowed, the response traffic is automatically allowed back out. A network access control list (network ACL) works at the subnet level, supports both allow and deny rules, and is stateless, so return traffic must be explicitly allowed. For example, to block one specific malicious IP address from an entire subnet, you would add a deny rule to the network ACL, because security groups cannot deny. Most applications rely mainly on security groups and keep network ACLs as a second layer. Remember instance level and stateful for security groups, subnet level and stateless for network ACLs.

concepts.heading: Where to Find Security Help and Products
concepts.body: AWS Trusted Advisor checks your account against best practices, and its security checks flag issues such as security groups open to the whole internet or the root user without MFA. AWS Marketplace offers third-party security products, such as firewalls and endpoint protection, that you can subscribe to and deploy in your account. For knowledge, the AWS Security Center, AWS Security Blog, AWS Knowledge Center articles, and AWS re:Post community answers explain how to implement security controls. AWS documentation also publishes security best practices for each service. Exam questions may ask where to find a third-party security tool (AWS Marketplace) or which service checks for open ports and missing MFA (Trusted Advisor).

examPoints: When a question describes finding PII in S3, pick Amazon Macie; scanning EC2 instances or container images for known software vulnerabilities, pick Amazon Inspector; detecting malicious activity from logs, pick Amazon GuardDuty.

When a question describes blocking SQL injection or filtering web requests by rule, pick AWS WAF; when it describes protecting against DDoS attacks, pick AWS Shield (Advanced if it mentions a response team or cost protection).

quiz.q: A company needs to automatically discover Amazon S3 objects that contain personally identifiable information such as passport numbers. Which service should it use?
quiz.explain: Amazon Macie is built to discover and classify sensitive data such as PII in Amazon S3. Amazon GuardDuty is tempting because it is also a security detection service, but it looks for malicious behavior in logs, not for sensitive content inside stored objects.

quiz.q: A web application behind an Application Load Balancer is receiving requests that attempt SQL injection. Which service can block these requests based on their content?
quiz.explain: AWS WAF inspects HTTP requests and can block patterns such as SQL injection before they reach the application. AWS Shield Standard is tempting because it protects web applications from attacks, but it defends against DDoS floods and does not inspect request content for injection attempts.

days.recap: GuardDuty detects threats, Inspector finds vulnerabilities, Macie finds sensitive data, Security Hub CSPM gathers findings, Shield stops DDoS, WAF filters web requests, and security groups (stateful) and network ACLs (stateless) control network traffic.

days.title: AWS Global Infrastructure and Ways to Deploy and Operate

concepts.heading: Regions and How to Choose One
concepts.body: An AWS Region is a separate geographic area, such as Asia Pacific (Seoul) or Europe (Frankfurt), and each Region is isolated from the others. Data you store in a Region stays there unless you choose to copy or move it, which matters for data residency laws. When choosing a Region, consider four factors: compliance and data governance requirements, proximity to customers for lower latency, which services and features are available in that Region, and pricing, which varies by Region. For example, a German bank with a rule that customer data must stay in the EU would choose an EU Region first and then check service availability. Compliance requirements usually outweigh the other factors.

concepts.heading: Availability Zones
concepts.body: Each Region contains multiple Availability Zones (AZs), and each AZ is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity. AZs in a Region are physically separated by a meaningful distance to reduce the chance that a single event such as a flood affects more than one, but they are connected by low-latency links. Deploying an application across at least two AZs is the standard way to achieve high availability. For example, placing EC2 instances in two AZs behind a load balancer keeps the application running if one AZ has a problem. Questions that ask how to protect against the failure of a single data center are pointing at Multi-AZ designs.

concepts.heading: Edge Locations and Extending AWS Closer to Users
concepts.body: Edge locations are sites in many cities worldwide that Amazon CloudFront uses to cache content close to viewers, and that Amazon Route 53 and AWS Global Accelerator also use. AWS Local Zones place compute and storage in large metropolitan areas so that latency-sensitive applications, such as video editing or real-time gaming, run very close to end users. AWS Wavelength embeds AWS infrastructure inside telecommunications providers' 5G networks for ultra-low latency mobile applications. AWS Outposts brings AWS-managed racks and servers into a customer's own data center, so workloads that must stay on premises can use the same AWS APIs and tools. Match the clue to the service: content caching is edge locations, a metropolitan area is Local Zones, 5G is Wavelength, and your own data center is Outposts.

concepts.heading: Ways to Access AWS
concepts.body: The AWS Management Console is the web interface, good for learning, exploring, and one-time tasks. The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) runs commands from a terminal, which makes tasks scriptable and repeatable, and AWS CloudShell provides a browser-based shell with the CLI already installed and authenticated. AWS SDKs let developers call AWS services from code written in languages such as Python, Java, and JavaScript. All of these call the same underlying AWS APIs. Exam questions about automating repetitive tasks point to the CLI or SDKs rather than the console.

concepts.heading: Infrastructure as Code
concepts.body: Infrastructure as code (IaC) means describing infrastructure in template files so it can be created the same way every time. AWS CloudFormation reads a JSON or YAML template and provisions all the described resources together as a stack, and it can update or delete that stack as one unit. The AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) lets developers define the same infrastructure in familiar programming languages and then generates CloudFormation templates. For example, a team can create identical development, test, and production environments in three Regions from one template. IaC reduces manual errors and supports the Well-Architected principle of performing operations as code.

examPoints: When a question asks which factors determine Region selection, pick compliance or data residency, latency to users, service availability, and pricing; when it asks how to survive a single data center failure, pick deploying across multiple Availability Zones.

When a question describes running AWS services inside the company's own data center, pick AWS Outposts; when it describes repeatable, template-based provisioning of resources, pick AWS CloudFormation.

quiz.q: A company must keep certain workloads in its own data center for regulatory reasons but wants to use the same AWS services, APIs, and tools it uses in the cloud. Which AWS offering meets this need?
quiz.explain: AWS Outposts delivers AWS-managed infrastructure into the customer's own facility, so the workload stays on premises while using AWS APIs. AWS Local Zones is tempting because it also places infrastructure closer to users, but Local Zones are AWS-operated sites in metropolitan areas, not the customer's own data center.

quiz.q: A team wants to create identical copies of its infrastructure for development, test, and production by using template files that can be version controlled. Which service should it use?
quiz.explain: AWS CloudFormation provisions resources from templates, so the same template creates identical stacks repeatedly. AWS Config is tempting because it deals with resource configuration, but it records and evaluates configurations; it does not create resources from templates.

days.recap: AWS runs Regions made of multiple Availability Zones plus edge locations, Local Zones, Wavelength, and Outposts, and you operate it through the console, CLI, SDKs, and infrastructure as code with CloudFormation.

days.title: Compute Services: EC2, Auto Scaling, Load Balancing, Lambda, and Containers

concepts.heading: Amazon EC2 and Instance Families
concepts.body: Amazon EC2 provides resizable virtual servers called instances, and you choose the operating system, instance type, storage, and network settings. Instance types are grouped into families by purpose: general purpose for balanced workloads such as web servers, compute optimized for CPU-heavy tasks such as batch processing or gaming servers, memory optimized for large in-memory databases, accelerated computing with GPUs for machine learning and graphics, and storage optimized for high, sequential disk throughput. An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is the template that contains the operating system and software used to launch an instance. Choosing the right family is part of rightsizing and the Performance Efficiency pillar. Questions often describe the workload and ask for the instance family.

concepts.heading: Auto Scaling and Elastic Load Balancing
concepts.body: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling adds or removes instances automatically to keep the right capacity, for example keeping average CPU near 50 percent or adding instances on a schedule before business hours. It also replaces unhealthy instances, which improves availability. Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets in multiple Availability Zones and sends traffic only to healthy targets. The Application Load Balancer routes HTTP and HTTPS requests and can route by URL path, while the Network Load Balancer handles very high volumes of TCP and UDP traffic with low latency. Together, a load balancer and an Auto Scaling group are the standard pattern for an elastic, highly available web tier.

concepts.heading: AWS Lambda and Serverless Computing
concepts.body: Serverless means you do not provision or manage servers; AWS runs the infrastructure, scales it automatically, and you pay only while your code runs. AWS Lambda runs your function code in response to events, such as a file uploaded to Amazon S3, a message in a queue, or an HTTP request through Amazon API Gateway. A single Lambda invocation can run for up to 15 minutes, so long-running jobs belong elsewhere. Pricing is based on the number of requests and the compute time used, so an idle function costs nothing. For example, a function that creates thumbnails whenever someone uploads a photo is a classic Lambda use case.

concepts.heading: Containers: ECS, EKS, Fargate, and ECR
concepts.body: Containers package an application with everything it needs to run, so it behaves the same on a laptop and in production. Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) is AWS's own container orchestration service, while Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) runs managed Kubernetes for teams that already use Kubernetes tools. Both can run containers on EC2 instances that you manage or on AWS Fargate, a serverless compute engine where you do not manage any servers at all. Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) stores your container images. If a question says the company already uses Kubernetes, pick EKS; if it says no servers to manage for containers, pick Fargate.

concepts.heading: Simpler Ways to Run Applications
concepts.body: AWS Elastic Beanstalk lets developers upload application code and automatically handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and health monitoring, while still allowing access to the underlying resources. Amazon Lightsail offers simple virtual private servers and bundles with a predictable monthly price, which suits small websites, blogs, and users new to the cloud. AWS Batch runs large numbers of batch computing jobs and chooses the right amount of compute for them. For example, a developer who wants to deploy a web application without learning about load balancers and Auto Scaling would use Elastic Beanstalk. These services trade some control for simplicity.

examPoints: When a question describes running short code in response to events with no servers to manage and no cost while idle, pick AWS Lambda; when it describes running containers without managing servers, pick AWS Fargate.

When a question describes automatically adding and removing EC2 instances based on demand, pick Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling; when it describes spreading traffic across healthy instances in several Availability Zones, pick Elastic Load Balancing.

quiz.q: A company wants to run code that resizes images each time a file is uploaded to Amazon S3. Each run takes a few seconds, and the company does not want to manage servers or pay for idle time. Which service fits best?
quiz.explain: Lambda runs short functions in response to events such as S3 uploads and charges only for the time the code runs. Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling is tempting because it scales, but the company would still manage servers and pay for at least some instances while no images are being uploaded.

quiz.q: A development team wants to run containerized applications without provisioning or managing any EC2 instances. Which service should it use with Amazon ECS?
quiz.explain: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers, so ECS tasks run without the team managing servers. Amazon ECR is tempting because it is also a container service, but it only stores container images and does not run them.

days.recap: EC2 gives you virtual servers in purpose-built families, Auto Scaling and load balancers make them elastic and highly available, Lambda runs event-driven code serverlessly, and ECS, EKS, and Fargate run containers.

days.title: Storage and Database Services: S3, EBS, EFS, RDS, Aurora, and DynamoDB

concepts.heading: Amazon S3 and Its Storage Classes
concepts.body: Amazon S3 is object storage: you store files as objects in buckets, it scales without limits you need to plan for, and it is designed for 99.999999999 percent (eleven nines) durability. Storage classes trade price against access speed: S3 Standard for frequently accessed data, S3 Intelligent-Tiering when access patterns are unknown, S3 Standard-Infrequent Access and S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access for data read rarely but needed quickly, and the Amazon S3 Glacier classes for archives. Within Glacier, Instant Retrieval returns data in milliseconds, Flexible Retrieval in minutes to hours, and Deep Archive, the cheapest class, typically within 12 hours. S3 Lifecycle rules can move objects to cheaper classes automatically as they age. One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, so it suits only data you can recreate.

concepts.heading: Block and File Storage: EBS, Instance Store, EFS, and FSx
concepts.body: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) provides block storage volumes that attach to an EC2 instance like a hard drive and persist after the instance stops; snapshots back them up to S3. Instance store is temporary block storage physically attached to the host, and its data is lost when the instance stops or terminates. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) is a managed file system for Linux that many instances in multiple Availability Zones can mount at the same time and that grows and shrinks automatically. Amazon FSx offers fully managed file systems such as FSx for Windows File Server and FSx for Lustre for high-performance computing. The key contrast is that an EBS volume normally attaches to one instance in one AZ, while EFS is shared by many.

concepts.heading: Hybrid Storage and Backup
concepts.body: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications to cloud storage, for example presenting a local file share whose files are stored in Amazon S3, or replacing physical backup tapes with virtual tapes in AWS. AWS Backup provides one central place to schedule, retain, and monitor backups across services such as EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, and FSx. Backup plans let you define rules such as daily backups kept for 35 days and copy them to another Region for disaster recovery. These services help companies use the cloud for storage without changing every application at once. A question about centrally managing backup policies across many AWS services points to AWS Backup.

concepts.heading: Relational Databases: Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora
concepts.body: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service supporting engines such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, and SQL Server, and AWS handles provisioning, patching, backups, and hardware. A Multi-AZ deployment keeps a standby in another Availability Zone and fails over automatically, which improves availability, while read replicas improve read performance. Amazon Aurora is AWS's cloud-built relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, offering higher performance and storage that is automatically replicated across three Availability Zones. Running a database yourself on EC2 gives more control but leaves patching and backups to you. Questions about reducing database administration effort for a relational workload usually point to RDS or Aurora.

concepts.heading: NoSQL and Purpose-Built Databases
concepts.body: Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless key-value and document database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, with no servers to manage and automatic scaling. Amazon ElastiCache provides in-memory caching with Valkey, Redis OSS, or Memcached to speed up applications by storing frequent query results in memory. Amazon Neptune is a graph database for highly connected data such as social networks or fraud rings, and Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) stores JSON documents. AWS encourages choosing a purpose-built database that fits the data model instead of forcing everything into one relational database. To move an existing database into any of these, AWS Database Migration Service is the tool.

examPoints: When a question asks for the cheapest storage for long-term archives that can wait hours to retrieve, pick S3 Glacier Deep Archive; when data must be retrieved in milliseconds but is rarely accessed, pick S3 Standard-IA or S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.

When a question describes a file system shared by many EC2 instances at once, pick Amazon EFS; when it describes a serverless NoSQL key-value database with millisecond latency at any scale, pick Amazon DynamoDB.

quiz.q: A company must keep compliance records for 10 years. The records are almost never read, and retrieval within 12 hours is acceptable. Which storage option has the lowest cost?
quiz.explain: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class and is designed for long-term retention with retrieval typically within 12 hours. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is tempting because it is also an archive class, but it costs more because it returns data in milliseconds, which this company does not need.

quiz.q: A mobile game needs a fully managed, serverless database that stores player profiles as key-value items and returns them in single-digit milliseconds even with millions of players. Which service fits best?
quiz.explain: DynamoDB is a serverless key-value database built for consistent millisecond performance at very large scale. Amazon RDS for MySQL is tempting because it is a managed database, but it is relational, runs on instances you size, and is not designed for serverless key-value access at this scale.

days.recap: Use S3 storage classes for objects, EBS for single-instance block storage, EFS for shared files, AWS Backup for central backups, RDS or Aurora for relational data, and DynamoDB or other purpose-built databases for other data models.

days.title: Networking and Content Delivery: VPC, Route 53, CloudFront, and Hybrid Connectivity

concepts.heading: Amazon VPC, Subnets, and Gateways
concepts.body: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) is your own logically isolated network in AWS, where you choose an IP address range and divide it into subnets in different Availability Zones. A public subnet has a route to an internet gateway, which lets resources with public IP addresses communicate with the internet. A private subnet has no such route, so resources there, such as databases, cannot be reached directly from the internet. A NAT gateway placed in a public subnet lets instances in private subnets start outbound connections, for example to download software updates, while still blocking inbound connections from the internet. Route tables decide where traffic from each subnet goes.

concepts.heading: Controlling Traffic Inside the VPC
concepts.body: Security groups and network ACLs, which you studied in the security domain, control traffic within a VPC: security groups at the resource level and network ACLs at the subnet level. VPC peering connects two VPCs so they can communicate privately, while AWS Transit Gateway acts as a central hub that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks, avoiding a complicated mesh of peering links. VPC endpoints let resources reach services such as Amazon S3 privately without going through the internet. For example, a company with 50 VPCs would use Transit Gateway rather than creating hundreds of peering connections. These details stay at a high level on CLF-C02, so focus on the purpose of each component.

concepts.heading: Amazon Route 53
concepts.body: Amazon Route 53 is AWS's highly available Domain Name System (DNS) service, which translates names like example.com into IP addresses. It can also register domain names and check the health of endpoints. Routing policies control how Route 53 answers queries: simple routing returns one answer, latency-based routing sends users to the Region with the lowest latency, geolocation routing chooses based on the user's location, weighted routing splits traffic by percentage, and failover routing sends traffic to a backup site when the primary is unhealthy. For example, failover routing can send users to a static maintenance site in S3 if the main application goes down. DNS questions on the exam point to Route 53.

concepts.heading: Amazon CloudFront and AWS Global Accelerator
concepts.body: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) that caches copies of static and dynamic content at edge locations around the world, so users download from a nearby location with lower latency. It works with origins such as S3 buckets and load balancers and integrates with AWS WAF and AWS Shield for protection. AWS Global Accelerator also uses the AWS edge network but does not cache content; instead it gives an application two static anycast IP addresses and routes users over the AWS global network to the best healthy endpoint. CloudFront is the choice for caching web content and media, while Global Accelerator is for improving performance and failover of non-cacheable TCP or UDP applications. Both reduce latency for a global audience.

concepts.heading: Connecting On-Premises Networks to AWS
concepts.body: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between an on-premises network and a VPC over the public internet, and it can be set up quickly at low cost. AWS Client VPN lets individual users connect securely from their laptops. AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network connection from a customer's data center or colocation facility to AWS, giving more consistent performance and higher bandwidth than internet-based connections. Direct Connect takes longer to set up because a physical connection is involved. Many companies use a VPN as a quick start or backup and Direct Connect for steady, high-volume traffic.

examPoints: When a question requires a dedicated, private connection with consistent network performance that does not travel over the public internet, pick AWS Direct Connect; when it requires a quick, encrypted connection over the internet, pick AWS Site-to-Site VPN.

When a question asks how instances in a private subnet can download updates from the internet without accepting inbound connections, pick a NAT gateway; when it asks how to cache content close to global users, pick Amazon CloudFront.

quiz.q: A company needs a private, dedicated network connection between its data center and AWS with consistent performance that does not use the public internet. Which service should it choose?
quiz.explain: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private connection with consistent performance outside the public internet. Site-to-Site VPN is tempting because it is also private and encrypted, but its tunnel runs over the public internet, so performance can vary.

quiz.q: Application servers in a private subnet must download operating system patches from the internet, but they must not be reachable from the internet. What should be added?
choices: A route from the private subnet directly to an internet gateway
A NAT gateway in a public subnet
quiz.explain: A NAT gateway lets private instances start outbound internet connections while blocking connections initiated from the internet. Routing the private subnet to an internet gateway is tempting because it gives internet access, but it would turn the subnet into a public subnet and could expose the servers.

days.recap: A VPC isolates your network with public and private subnets, Route 53 handles DNS, CloudFront and Global Accelerator speed up global users, and Site-to-Site VPN or Direct Connect link your data center to AWS.

days.title: Analytics, AI/ML, Application Integration, and Other Service Categories

concepts.heading: Analytics Services
concepts.body: Amazon Athena runs standard SQL queries directly on data stored in Amazon S3 without loading it anywhere, and you pay per query based on the data scanned. Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for fast analytics on large volumes of structured data, used for business reporting across many years of records. AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service that discovers data, keeps a data catalog, and runs extract, transform, and load (ETL) jobs. Amazon EMR runs big data frameworks such as Apache Spark and Hadoop, and Amazon OpenSearch Service supports log analytics and search. For dashboards, Amazon QuickSight creates interactive business intelligence visualizations; AWS now offers it as Quick Sight inside the Amazon Quick workspace, but exam questions use the QuickSight name.

concepts.heading: Streaming Data
concepts.body: Streaming data arrives continuously, such as clickstreams, IoT sensor readings, or application logs. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams captures and stores streaming data so custom applications can process it in real time. Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) is the easiest way to load streaming data into destinations such as Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, or Amazon OpenSearch Service, with no code to manage. Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) runs Apache Kafka for teams that already use it. A question that says load streaming data into S3 with minimal management points to Data Firehose, while real-time custom processing points to Kinesis Data Streams.

concepts.heading: AI and Machine Learning Services
concepts.body: Amazon SageMaker AI is the managed service for building, training, and deploying your own machine learning models. AWS also offers ready-made AI services that need no ML expertise: Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video, Amazon Comprehend finds meaning and sentiment in text, Amazon Textract extracts text and tables from scanned documents, Amazon Transcribe turns speech into text, Amazon Polly turns text into speech, Amazon Translate translates languages, and Amazon Lex builds chatbots. For generative AI, Amazon Bedrock gives API access to foundation models from Amazon and other providers. Amazon Q offers generative AI assistants, such as Amazon Q Developer for helping with code and AWS tasks; Amazon Q Business (answers from company data) and Amazon Kendra (enterprise search), found in older materials, closed to new customers in July 2026.

concepts.heading: Application Integration
concepts.body: Application integration services let components communicate without depending directly on each other, which is loose coupling. Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) is a message queue: producers put messages in the queue and consumers process them at their own pace, so nothing is lost when the consumer is slow or temporarily down. Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) is publish and subscribe messaging that pushes one message to many subscribers at once, such as email, SMS, Lambda functions, or SQS queues. Amazon EventBridge routes events from AWS services, your applications, and SaaS partners to targets based on rules, and AWS Step Functions coordinates multiple steps into a visual workflow. The key contrast is queue and pull for SQS versus fan-out push for SNS.

concepts.heading: Other Service Categories
concepts.body: CLF-C02 also expects you to recognize a few services from other categories. Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center service for customer engagement, and Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) sends marketing and transactional email. Amazon WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops for end-user computing, and Amazon WorkSpaces Applications (formerly Amazon AppStream 2.0) streams desktop applications to a browser. AWS Amplify helps front-end web and mobile developers build and host full-stack applications, and AWS IoT Core connects billions of devices to the cloud. For developer tools, AWS CodeBuild compiles and tests code, AWS CodePipeline automates release pipelines, and AWS X-Ray traces requests through distributed applications.

examPoints: When a question describes querying data in S3 with SQL without loading it into a database, pick Amazon Athena; when it describes a data warehouse for complex reporting on large structured datasets, pick Amazon Redshift.
When a question describes buffering messages so a slow consumer can process them later, pick Amazon SQS; when it describes sending one message to many subscribers at once, pick Amazon SNS.

quiz.q: A data analyst wants to run SQL queries on log files stored in Amazon S3 without loading them into a database or managing servers, paying only for the queries run. Which service should the analyst use?
quiz.explain: Athena queries data in place in S3 using SQL, is serverless, and charges per query. Amazon Redshift is tempting because it is AWS's main SQL analytics service, but it is a data warehouse that normally requires loading data and running a cluster or serverless workgroup, which is more than this analyst needs.

quiz.q: An order-processing application must keep accepting orders even when the backend processing service is slow or briefly unavailable. Which service should sit between the two components to hold the orders until they are processed?
quiz.explain: Amazon SQS stores messages durably in a queue until a consumer processes them, decoupling the producer from a slow or failed consumer. Amazon SNS is tempting because it also passes messages between components, but it pushes messages immediately to subscribers and does not hold them for later processing on its own.

days.recap: Athena, Redshift, Glue, Kinesis, and Data Firehose cover analytics, SageMaker AI and the ready-made AI services plus Bedrock and Amazon Q cover AI, and SQS, SNS, and EventBridge decouple applications.

days.title: Pricing Models, Billing Tools, and AWS Support Options

concepts.heading: Compute Purchasing Options
concepts.body: On-Demand Instances are billed by the second or hour with no commitment, which suits short-term, unpredictable workloads and testing. Savings Plans give a discount of up to 72 percent in exchange for committing to a consistent amount of usage, measured in dollars per hour, for one or three years; Compute Savings Plans apply across EC2 instance families, Regions, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda, while EC2 Instance Savings Plans give a deeper discount for a chosen instance family in one Region. Reserved Instances also give up to 72 percent off for a one- or three-year commitment to specific instance attributes, and you can pay all upfront, partial upfront, or no upfront, with more upfront meaning a bigger discount. Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at up to 90 percent off, but AWS can reclaim them with a two-minute warning, so they suit flexible, fault-tolerant jobs such as batch processing. Dedicated Hosts give you a whole physical server, often for licensing that is tied to physical cores.

concepts.heading: Estimating and Tracking Costs
concepts.body: The AWS Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of an architecture before you build it. AWS Cost Explorer visualizes past and current spending, filters it by service, account, or tag, and forecasts future costs. AWS Budgets lets you set custom cost, usage, or Savings Plans coverage budgets and sends alerts when actual or forecasted amounts cross a threshold. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to spot unusual spending and notify you, and AWS Data Exports delivers the detailed Cost and Usage Report data to Amazon S3 for deep analysis. Cost allocation tags, such as a project or department tag, let you break down the bill by team.

concepts.heading: AWS Organizations Consolidated Billing
concepts.body: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations combines the charges of all member accounts into one bill paid by the management account. Usage is added together across accounts, so the organization reaches volume pricing tiers, such as lower per-gigabyte S3 prices, sooner than accounts would on their own. Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts can also be shared across accounts in the organization. Consolidated billing itself has no extra charge. A question about combining bills from many accounts and gaining volume discounts points to AWS Organizations.

concepts.heading: AWS Support Plans
concepts.body: Basic Support is free for every account and includes billing and account help, documentation, AWS re:Post, the AWS Health Dashboard, and a core set of AWS Trusted Advisor checks. In December 2025 AWS introduced a new lineup of paid plans: Business Support+ adds 24/7 access to AWS engineers with AI-assisted troubleshooting and the full set of Trusted Advisor checks, Enterprise Support adds a designated technical account manager (TAM) and faster response, and Unified Operations adds the fastest response and a wider team of specialists. AWS lists critical-case response targets of 30 minutes for Business Support+, 15 minutes for Enterprise Support, and as fast as 5 minutes for Unified Operations. The older Developer, Business, and Enterprise On-Ramp plans are being discontinued on January 1, 2027, but the CLF-C02 exam and older practice questions may still use the old lineup: Basic, Developer, Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, and Enterprise. The lasting rules are that the full Trusted Advisor checks start at the business-level plan (Business or Business Support+) and a designated TAM requires Enterprise Support (Enterprise On-Ramp offered only a pool of TAMs).

concepts.heading: Other Sources of Help
concepts.body: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your account and recommends improvements in cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits, and operational excellence, such as idle load balancers or underused instances. The AWS Health Dashboard shows AWS service events and, in your account view, events that affect your own resources, such as scheduled maintenance. AWS re:Post is a community question-and-answer site moderated with AWS experts, and the AWS Knowledge Center answers common questions. AWS Marketplace is a curated catalog of third-party software, data, and services you can buy and deploy, often billed on your AWS bill. For hands-on help, the AWS Partner Network (APN) lists consulting and technology partners, and AWS Professional Services and AWS Solutions Architects assist with larger projects.

examPoints: When a question describes steady usage for one or three years with flexibility across instance families, Regions, Fargate, or Lambda, pick Compute Savings Plans; when it describes interruptible, flexible batch jobs at the lowest price, pick Spot Instances.

When a question asks to estimate costs before building, pick AWS Pricing Calculator; to analyze past spending, pick AWS Cost Explorer; to get an alert when spending crosses a threshold, pick AWS Budgets.

quiz.q: A company runs steady workloads 24/7 and expects to keep them for three years, but it plans to move some of them from EC2 to AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda. Which pricing option gives a discount while keeping that flexibility?
quiz.explain: Compute Savings Plans discount steady usage under a one- or three-year commitment and apply across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda. Spot Instances are tempting because they are cheaper, but they can be interrupted at any time, which does not suit steady 24/7 workloads.

quiz.q: A finance manager wants to receive an email when the forecasted monthly AWS spend for a project is expected to exceed $500. Which service should be used?
quiz.explain: AWS Budgets sends alerts when actual or forecasted costs cross a threshold you set. Cost Explorer is tempting because it shows forecasts, but it is a reporting and analysis tool and does not send threshold alerts on its own.

days.recap: Match pricing to usage (On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved, Spot), use Pricing Calculator, Cost Explorer, and Budgets to estimate, analyze, and alert, consolidate bills with Organizations, and know that full Trusted Advisor starts at the business-level support plan and a TAM needs Enterprise.

days.title: Final Review: Practice Exam, Confused Service Pairs, and Exam-Day Strategy

concepts.heading: Know the Exam Format
concepts.body: CLF-C02 has 65 questions to answer in 90 minutes: 50 are scored and 15 are unscored questions that AWS is testing and that are not marked. Results are reported on a scaled score from 100 to 1,000, and the passing score is 700. Questions are either multiple choice with one correct answer or multiple response with two or more correct answers, and there is no penalty for guessing, so never leave a question blank. The domain weights are Cloud Technology and Services 34 percent, Security and Compliance 30 percent, Cloud Concepts 24 percent, and Billing, Pricing, and Support 12 percent. Take one timed practice set today under these conditions to check your pacing.

concepts.heading: Review the Most Confused Service Pairs
concepts.body: Most foundational mistakes come from a small number of look-alike services. CloudTrail records who made API calls, Config tracks resource settings and compliance, and CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs. GuardDuty detects threats from logs, Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, and Macie finds sensitive data in S3. Shield stops DDoS attacks, while WAF filters web requests by rule; security groups are stateful and instance-level, while network ACLs are stateless and subnet-level. Pricing Calculator estimates future costs, Cost Explorer analyzes past costs, and Budgets sends alerts.

concepts.heading: Revisit the Shared Responsibility Model and Pricing
concepts.body: Security and Compliance is nearly a third of the exam, and the shared responsibility model appears in many disguises. Rehearse it with three services: on EC2 the customer patches the guest operating system, on RDS AWS patches the engine but the customer controls access, and on Lambda the customer owns only code, permissions, and data. For pricing, connect each model to its workload: On-Demand for short or unpredictable use, Savings Plans or Reserved Instances for steady long-term use, and Spot for interruptible jobs. For support, remember that a designated TAM needs Enterprise Support and Basic includes only core Trusted Advisor checks. If any of these still feel shaky, reread days 4 and 13.

concepts.heading: Use an Error Log
concepts.body: For every practice question you miss or guess, write down the pair of ideas you confused, such as Rehost versus Replatform or Direct Connect versus Site-to-Site VPN. Reviewing these pairs is faster than rereading every day of the guide, because the same confusions tend to repeat. Spend the most time on the domains with the highest weight unless your error log shows a specific weak area. Read the scenario for the deciding keyword, such as serverless, dedicated connection, sensitive data, or lowest cost, before looking at the choices. Then eliminate choices that solve a different problem.

concepts.heading: Exam-Day Strategy
concepts.body: Make a first pass through all 65 questions, answer the ones you know, and flag any you are unsure about so you can return later. With 90 minutes you have a little under 1.5 minutes per question, which is plenty for most foundational questions if you do not get stuck. Watch for words such as most cost-effective, least operational overhead, or managed, because AWS exams usually reward the fully managed, purpose-built service. For multiple response questions, check how many answers are required and choose exactly that many. Finally, make sure every question has an answer before you submit.

examPoints: When a question asks for the least operational overhead and two answers would both work, pick the fully managed or serverless AWS service rather than one you would run yourself on EC2.

When a question asks about security responsibilities, first decide whether the item is the cloud itself (facilities, hardware, managed service infrastructure, which is AWS) or something placed in the cloud (data, access, configuration, which is the customer).

quiz.q: Which AWS Support plan includes a designated technical account manager (TAM)?
quiz.explain: Enterprise Support includes a designated TAM who provides proactive guidance. Business Support+ is tempting because it adds 24/7 access to engineers and the full set of Trusted Advisor checks, but it does not include a designated TAM.

quiz.q: A security team wants to automatically scan its Amazon EC2 instances and container images in Amazon ECR for known software vulnerabilities. Which service should it use?
quiz.explain: Amazon Inspector scans EC2 instances, container images, and Lambda functions for known software vulnerabilities. Amazon GuardDuty is tempting because it is also a security detection service, but it looks for malicious activity in logs rather than vulnerable software packages.

days.recap: Know the format (65 questions, 90 minutes, 700 to pass), drill the confused service pairs, rehearse shared responsibility and pricing models, and pick the managed, purpose-built service when in doubt.
